topic.title: Network Diffusion, Influence, and Latent Structure
topic.area: Graphical Models, Clustering, and Network Structure
topic.overview: Network diffusion models describe how activity or information spreads between connected entities. This topic studies learning those dynamics from partial observations, estimating influence, and selecting interventions. A representative method uses dynamic message passing to learn an effective cascade model from limited activation-time information, optimizing the quality of predictions needed for downstream control.
topic.whyItMatters: Incomplete observations make the underlying network and spreading process uncertain. A model useful for forecasting or intervention must account for that uncertainty rather than assuming that observed cascades directly reveal every connection or transmission probability.
topic.evolution: The representatives develop diffusion-network inference and scalable influence estimation, followed by sample-based learning and community-aware influence methods. Recent work addresses online feedback and simulation transfer. Related latent-network theory examines how choosing an incorrect embedding dimension affects structural estimation.
openQuestions: When do accurate marginal predictions suffice for reliable interventions?
How can influence methods remain effective when network structure and propagation mechanisms change together?
